A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Effort and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably despite reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original deepfake and synthetic-image detection results, ablations, robustness tests, and feature analyses, including GenImage experiments in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports rank/accuracy comparisons and self-attention analyses in Table 8 and Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: The SVD decomposition, frozen principal components, trainable residual components, and classification, orthogonality, and singular-value losses remain unchanged in Equations 1–7. Algorithm 1 moves from v2's Appendix B into v3's methodology with an equivalent return step.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same deepfake benchmarks, UniversalFakeDetect, and GenImage coverage. The new attention examples use CycleGAN, ProGAN, DeepFakes, and LDM images already represented in the existing evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched benchmark and ablation tables. TALL is newly named in v3's main-text discussion, but Table 1 gains no TALL row; TALL-Swin already appeared in v2's appendix video comparison. The added diagnostics use previously compared models.

E3.justification: The new attention analysis compares CLS-to-patch attention across 24 CLIP blocks using combined and separate original/LoRA or principal/residual weights. This adds a diagnostic procedure and controls; existing detection splits, frame sampling, training settings, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 8 extends the existing PCA analysis with rank/accuracy comparisons across face and general-image domains. Appendix C.2 and Figures 11–14 add layerwise attention case studies examining semantic preservation and forgery separation. Existing component, rank, backbone, and perturbation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the detection results. The added diagnostics retain point estimates and qualitative visualizations.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation table values are retained. v3 corrects Section 4.3 to match the unchanged Table 4, including baseline AUC 0.854 to 0.859 and full-model AUC 0.921 to 0.941. Table 8 and the attention analyses add diagnostic results, including the reported concentration of semantic information in earlier blocks.

T1.justification: v3 removes Definition 3.1's covariance-asymmetry measure, Theorem 3.2 and its assumptions and rank bound, and the proof in v2's Appendix A. The SVD mathematics remains. The new Rademacher-complexity discussion provides conceptual motivation without a replacement theorem or derivation.

C1.justification: v3 makes the claim that Effort implicitly models a hierarchical relationship between real and fake images central to its abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion. This replaces the performance-focused fourth contribution with a claimed generalization insight, while retaining the method and superior-detection claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds a substantive mechanism explanation: the real-to-fake hierarchy enables discrimination within semantically aligned subspaces with reduced model complexity. It also explains the low residual-rank choice through limited forgery diversity and binary classification, and interprets the new attention maps as semantic/forgery separation. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly documents the choice n-r=1 and adds a public-code statement and GitHub link. v2 only promises release upon acceptance; that future-release wording also remains in v3's appendix. The principal training implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Mohri and Rostamizadeh (2008) to support the complexity discussion and Yan et al. (2025), GPT-ImgEval, to the introduction. The related-work survey and positioning against existing detectors otherwise remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, introduction, and conclusion receive targeted revisions, with expanded baseline and rank-choice explanations. Algorithm 1 moves into the methodology, the appendices are reorganized, and affiliations, correspondence information, and acknowledgments are updated. Much of the prose remains verbatim.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual material with Table 8 and four new attention-map grids, Figures 11–14. The existing CycleGAN visualization moves from v2's Figure 10 to v3's Figure 4 with a revised caption. The algorithm, retained plots, and tables are redistributed throughout the document.

improvement.justification: Correcting the ablation discussion to match Table 4 and adding rank/attention diagnostics improve empirical clarity and transparency. Bringing the algorithm into the methodology and adding a code pointer also help readers. These are limited gains: benchmark outcomes are unchanged, and the removed theorem and proof are replaced by a hierarchical-prior explanation that remains informal.
